Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Orlando ...

Reference the attached letter dated April 20, 1938
from the British Consulate-General, requesting information
concerning Carlos Orlando Danenberg alias Orly, British
Subject (Eurasian), this person first came to the notice
of the S.M.P. during 1930, when he lodged a complaint
against one M. Roubin, to the effect that the latter had
snatched a satchel from him, containing photographs, etc.,
valued at $200.00. In the course of enquiries into
this matter it was learned that Roubin was in debt to
Danenberg and in the absence of evidence to support the
charge of snatching, it was strongly believed that the
complaint made by Danenberg was baseless and merely a
manoeuvre calculated to bring pressure on Roubin to cause
him to settle the debt mentioned above.

Some time between 1925 and 1930, Danenberg married
a Russian named Helena Yaokvlevna Camarmetz, from whom he
separated shortly afterwards.

Danenberg was next heard of on December 23, 1935,
when one C. Schroeter (German), member of the Seventh Day
Adventist Mission, 26, Ying Ts Loo, Hangchow, Chekiang,
made a complaint to the S.M.P., at Hongkew Station, to
the effect that about the end of August, 1935, he entrusted
his camera, which he valued at $200.00, to Danenberg, in
Hangchow, on the understanding that the latter would
endeavour to sell it for him. Danenberg took the camera
to Shanghai the next day and later returned to Hangchow
without it, explaining to Schroeter that he had left it

参照附件中英国总领事馆于1938年4月20日来信，要求提供关于 Carlos Orlando Danenberg（别名 Orly），英国籍人士（欧亚混血）的情报。此人首次进入上海公共租界工部局警务处视线是在1930年，当时他对一名 M. Roubin 提出控告，称后者抢走了他的一个手提包，内有照片等物，价值200.00美元。在对此事进行调查的过程中，获悉 Roubin 欠 Danenberg 债务，且由于缺乏支持抢劫指控的证据，警方强烈认为 Danenberg 的控告毫无根据，仅仅是为了向 Roubin 施压以迫使其偿还上述债务而采取的一种手段。

在1925年至1930年间的某个时候，Danenberg 与一名名为 Helena Yaokvlevna Camarmetz 的俄罗斯女子结婚，但不久后便分居。

下一次听到有关 Danenberg 的消息是在1935年12月23日，当时浙江杭州英士路26号基督复临安息日会传教团的一名成员 C. Schroeter（德国人）向虹口巡捕房提出控告，称大约在1935年8月底，他在杭州将自己的相机托付给 Danenberg，约定由后者代为出售，该相机估值200.00美元。Danenberg 次日将相机带至上海，随后空手返回杭州，并向 Schroeter 解释说他将相机留给了

The camera was subsequently found by Schroeter

At the time of writing this report the S.M.P.

British Supreme Court for China, at Shanghai, on April 2,

connection with this case, that Danenberg succeeded in
ingratiating himself into the confidence of a Siamese,
namely, Chnar Anusara Soondora, wealthy doctor, at present
visiting Shanghai, and after inducing him to engage

banking code.
Danenberg's passport was not lost in the interior

BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL,
P.O. BOX 259. SHANGHAI.

20th April, 1938.

Dear Bourne.

A certain Carlos Orlando Lenenberg, arrived in
Hongkong on 2.4.38. He stated that he was connected with the
Chinese Government as an aerial photographer and had just
arrived from the interior of China. He stated that his property,
which contained his passport, was left behind in a town which is
now occupied by the Japanese and he has, therefore, little hope
of recovering it. He claims to have been born in Hongkong on
26.9.91 and produced a copy of the Hongkong birth registration
in support of this. He further stated that he was connected with
the L'Asis Photograph Studio, Gloucester Arcade, and would stay
in Hongkong for a few weeks.

A source (who may well be unreliable) has stated that
Lenenberg has a criminal record in Shanghai and may also have
some political connection with the Japanese.

I would be most grateful for any information you
can let me have about this man.

Yours sincerely,

[Signature]

Major K. M. Bourne, M.C.
Shanghai Municipal Police.

CONFIDENTIAL
DANENBERG

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. F. 1825
M. C. D. 1911
Date .../.../...

Danenberg Is Sentenced To
One Month In Gaol

Complex Larceny Case Brought To Close In Local
British Court; Magistrate Says He Could Not
Believe Story Of Camel Hair Overcoat

Sentence of one month's imprisonment at Ward Road Gaol, was passed on Carlos Orlando Danenberg, by Magistrate C. H. Haines in H.M. Police Court yesterday, when the accused was found guilty on charges of having stolen a camel-hair overcoat and a scarf from Dr. Edward Charles Coolidge, a Siamese subject, also known as Dr. Soondora.

The verdict which was meted out yesterday, brought to a close one of the longest and most complex larceny cases ever tried locally. The latter difficulty arose chiefly over the large number of witnesses which were produced throughout the hearings and the varying degrees of evidence which was received. As an example of this, James Roope, one of the principal witnesses for the prosecution, was finally treated as a "hostile" witness by the prosecutor Mr. Watkin Williams, when it was disclosed that he had passed on a statement to Mr. R. L. Stuart, counsel for the defence.

Original complaints filed in the case alleged that Danenberg had stolen property to the value of $1,000, together with a passport from the Siamese doctor. However the magistrate was unable to find sufficient cause to support the prosecution with regard to the missing property other than the coat and scarf.

Lied Stupidly

In summing up his decision, the magistrate declared that although the accused might possibly have travelled to Hongkong unintentionally, his subsequent actions with the scarf and coat were tantamount to conversion of it to his own use. Continuing, Mr. Haines said: "Frankly, I don't believe his (Danenberg's) story that he left the coat with a dry-cleaner when he returned to Shanghai. His demeanour in the box was such that I was convinced that he was lying all the time—and he lied stupidly. I am quite certain that he did steal the overcoat, and I have no confidence whatever in the accused's statements. My conclusion is that he did steal the coat and scarf and that he has been endeavouring to explain away his conduct."

At this point Mr. Watkin Williams asked if the court wished to hear further police information regarding the accused's past, stating that such was a usual course in cases of a similar nature prior to the passing of sentence.

Detective Inspector Crighton of the Shanghai Municipal Police was called and stated that Danenberg first came to the notice of the police when he laid a false charge against a man named Ruben in November, 1930, which was subsequently withdrawn. Later a charge in connection with the theft of a camera from Hangchow was made against the accused, but this was also withdrawn. Among the papers found on Danenberg's person when he was arrested by the police, was a deportation order from Canada.

First Conviction

Mr. Haines said: "This deportation order was made to prevent him from becoming a public charge." Addressing Danenberg, Mr. Haines continued: "What I have just heard has not made any difference to what I was going to do with you. This is the first recorded conviction against you here, and, as I said before, I am going to take into consideration that you have already spent nearly three weeks under remand in custody.

"Nevertheless, the theft was a particularly mean one and you have not improved it by the lies you have told in the box. I did not believe you at all. You will be sentenced to one month's imprisonment, from to-day."

Earlier during the hearing, Mr. R. L. Stuart, counsel for the defence, called Mr. Ilagin, an additional witness, to give evidence in regard to two letters which Danenberg said he sent from Hongkong. The witness denied that he had received any letters from Danenberg, but said that when the accused returned to Shanghai, he mentioned the letters and said that they contained an explanation of how he had sailed for Hongkong, and referred to Dr. Coolidge's coat and passport.

Mr. Stuart then re-examined Danenberg, in connection with the contents of the letters. Danenberg replied that the first was a request to Mr. Ilagin to forward his funds in order to return to Shanghai, while the second, which he claimed to have mailed "poste restante" in Shanghai, asked why the first letter had not been replied to.

Wanted Instructions

Describing the contents of another letter which he said had been sent from Hongkong to Dr. Coolidge, Danenberg said that this letter also referred to the overcoat and passport, and asked Dr. Coolidge for instructions regarding them.

In reply to cross-examination by Mr. Watkin Williams, Danenberg declared that the letters to Ilagin and Coolidge had been written two or three days after he arrived in Hongkong. The second letter to Ilagin was sent not more than a week later.

"Why didn't you tell the Hongkong police that you wanted to return to Shanghai," asked Mr. Williams. Danenberg replied that he did, and although he had not mentioned it in his statement to the police, they knew it.

"I put it to you that your whole story is a fabrication; that you have never sent the coat to the cleaners and that you disposed of it," the prosecutor declared. "No, sir," replied Danenberg.

When sentence was finally declared by the magistrate, the accused turned tear-stained eyes around the court, then straightened himself and walked out of the courtroom in the custody of a police gaoler.

Danenberg 被判
入狱一个月

复杂的盗窃案在地方法院审结；法官表示无法相信关于骆驼毛大衣的说辞

昨日，在英国皇家警察法庭，法官 C. H. Haines 判处 Carlos Orlando Danenberg 华德路监狱监禁一个月，被告被裁定犯有从暹罗籍人士 Edward Charles Coolidge 博士（又名 Soondora 博士）处窃取一件骆驼毛大衣和一条围巾的罪名。

昨日作出的判决终结了本地审理过的最漫长、最复杂的盗窃案之一。后期的困难主要源于庭审过程中传唤的大量证人以及所获证据的各种差异。例如，控方主要证人之一 James Roope 最终被控方律师 Watkin Williams 先生视为“敌意”证人，因为披露出他曾向辩方律师 R. L. Stuart 先生传递过一份陈述。

本案最初提交的控告称，Danenberg 窃取了价值1,000美元的财产以及那位暹罗医生的护照。然而，法官认为除大衣和围巾外，没有足够的理由支持控方关于其他丢失财产的指控。

愚蠢地撒谎

在总结判决时，法官宣布，虽然被告可能是无意中前往香港，但他随后对围巾和大衣的处理等同于将其据为己用。Haines 先生接着说：“坦率地说，我不相信他（Danenberg）的说法，即他回到上海时将大衣留在了干洗店。他在证人席上的表现让我确信他一直在撒谎——而且撒得很拙劣。我十分肯定他确实偷了那件大衣，我对被告的陈述毫无信心。我的结论是他确实偷了大衣和围巾，并且一直试图为自己的行为辩解。”

此时，Watkin Williams 先生询问法庭是否希望听取有关被告过往的更多警方情报，指出在类似案件宣判前，这通常是常规程序。

上海公共租界工部局警务处的侦探督察 Crighton 出庭作证，称 Danenberg 首次引起警方注意是在1930年11月，当时他对一名名为 Ruben 的男子提出虚假指控，随后撤诉。后来，被告又因涉嫌在杭州盗窃相机而被指控，但该指控也被撤销。在警方逮捕 Danenberg 时，从其身上发现的文件中有一份来自加拿大的驱逐令。

首次定罪

Haines 先生说：“这份驱逐令是为了防止他成为公共负担。” Haines 先生接着对 Danenberg 说：“我刚才听到的情况并没有改变我打算对你做出的处理。这是你在这里的第一次有记录的定罪，而且，正如我之前所说，我会考虑到你已经在还押候审期间被拘留了近三个星期。

“尽管如此，这次盗窃行为特别卑鄙，而且你在证人席上的谎言并没有改善你的处境。我根本不相信你。你将从今天起被判处一个月监禁。”

在庭审较早阶段，辩方律师 R. L. Stuart 先生传唤了额外证人 Mr. Ilagin，就 Danenberg 声称从香港寄出的两封信件作证。该证人否认收到过 Danenberg 的任何信件，但表示当被告回到上海时，提到了这些信件，并称信中解释了他如何乘船前往香港，并提到了 Coolidge 博士的大衣和护照。

随后，Stuart 先生就信件内容再次讯问 Danenberg。Danenberg 回答说，第一封信是请求 Ilagin 先生汇寄资金以便他返回上海，而第二封信是他声称在上海以“存局候领”方式寄出的，询问为何第一封信没有收到回复。

寻求指示

Danenberg 在描述另一封据称从香港寄给 Coolidge 博士的信件内容时说，这封信也提到了大衣和护照，并请 Coolidge 博士就此给予指示。

在回答 Watkin Williams 先生的交叉质询时，Danenberg 声称给 Ilagin 和 Coolidge 的信是在他抵达香港两三天后写的。给 Ilagin 的第二封信是在不超过一周后寄出的。

“你为什么不告诉香港警察你想回上海？”Williams 先生问道。Danenberg 回答说他说过了，虽然他在给警方的陈述中没有提到这一点，但警方知道此事。

“我要指出，你的整个故事都是捏造的；你从未把大衣送去清洗，而是把它处理掉了，”控方律师宣称。“不，先生，”Danenberg 回答道。

当法官最终宣判时，被告含着泪环顾法庭，然后挺直身子，在警察狱卒的看守下走出法庭。

海恩斯（C. H. Haines）推事指出，他将与法官商谈，看是否有可能为被告获取法律援助，并于昨日上午在英国警务法庭再次延期审理卡洛斯·奥兰多·丹嫩伯格（Carlos Orlando Danenberg）被控盗窃一案。

当丹嫩伯格在对本案原告、暹罗医生库利奇（G. F. Coolidge）博士进行交叉讯问时陷入混乱，海恩斯推事遂中止了诉讼程序。

海恩斯推事将案件延期至下周三，丹嫩伯格再次被还押候审。P. 沃特金·威廉姆斯（P. Watkin Williams）先生代表检方出庭。

Danenberg's 2nd Appearance
Prosecution Continues in Larceny Charges
Against Briton ; Visit to Empress Liner

EVIDENCE as to how the accused boarded the Canadian Pacific
liner Empress of Japan—ostensibly to say goodbye to a girl-
friend—and remained on board until after the vessel had sailed,
was given in H.M. Police Cou. before Mr. C. H. Haines, Registrar,
yesterday, when Carlos Orlando Danenberg, a British subject of
Hongkong, made his second appearance, charged with the larceny
of certain money and property to the value of $1,000, belonging
to Dr. C. A. Soondora, a Siamese physician educated in London.
Mr. F. Watkin Williams appeared for the prosecution, while
Danenberg was not represented.

James Roope, aged 26, a cook of
no fixed abode, said that he first met
Danenberg in September 1935 at a
Salvation Army Hostel, where the
accused was living at the time. Later
the witness, after staying ten days
with his brother, went to the Yangtze
Hotel at the corner of Hankow and
Yunnan Roads. Here he was in-
troduced to two men by Danenberg,
one of whom was Dr. Soondora,
who was introduced in the name of
Dr. Coolidge.

The other person was known as
Mr. Liang. A few days later, he
was asked by Danenberg to stay
with him at Room 519, Yangtze
Hotel, and, in company with Dr.
Coolidge, Mr. Liang, Mr. Ilagan and
the accused, he stayed there from
February 20 until April 18.

The accused also used Room 211
at the hotel as a sort of private
office, and later as a living room for
Dr. Coolidge. On the evening of
March 22, the accused and the wit-
ness were walking around the pass-
age way for about an hour discussing
the question of the rent of Room
211. Danenberg told him that it
amounted to $109 and that it
would be paid, adding that he would
do his best to raise the money. Later
he remarked "Don't worry, Jim. it
isn't much money after all, and I
can always get money if I want it."
The accused then showed the witness
a pile of money, adding "I don't
quite want to pay for the room
right now as I want Dr. Coolidge...."
At this stage the witness hesitated,
and, on being questioned said that
he did not know whether they were
Danenberg's exact words. The sen-
tence was then struck out.

Continuing, the witness said that
it was Danenberg's idea to hold up
payment for the room for a time to
make Dr. Coolidge feel sorry, hoping
that Dr. Coolidge would try and raise
money to pay the rent of the room.
Danenberg left Shanghai on March
23, and about a fortnight before this
date he noticed that the accused
possessed the passport of Dr.
Coolidge which, he said, had been
given to him for safe keeping. On
the evening of March 22 the Yangtze
Hotel No. 1 Floor Boy came into
Room 519 and asked Danenberg for
the rent of Room 211 and he answer-
ed "Wait." The rent was paid later.
On March 22 Dr. Coolidge had to
sleep out of his Room 211 as it had
been locked.

Girl Friend

A request by Danenberg to the wit-
ness to accompany him to see a girl
friend off on the Empress of Japan
was made on March 23. When the
accused came into Room 619, where
Mr. Ilagan and Dr. Coolidge were
sleeping soundly he was wearing a
camel hair overcoat. He locked the
door when they left the room and
they proceeded to Room 211. Here

the accused moved about in an ex-
cited manner, and told the witness
that he could use Dr. Coolidge's
raincoat. A scarf belonging to the
doctor was taken by Danenberg,
while the camel hair overcoat, also
belonged to this person.

From the hotel they went to the
Sun Co. to buy a present, for which
Danenberg paid $5.50, for the girl
friend, and from there to the Shang-
hai and Hongkew Wharf where they
boarded the Empress of Japan.

At the reception desk Danenberg
asked for the cabin of a person
named Sung, the witness being led
to believe that the girl friend's name
was Miss Mary Sung. They were
told that the person was in cabin
425, but on going there they did not
see anybody. After looking around
the boat together, Danenberg asked
the witness to stay at the cabin
while he looked around upstairs.
During this time the gong and siren
went to summon non-passengers
ashore, and running through the
ship the witness was able to get on
to the wharf. He immediately made
his way to the Customs Jetty in
order to meet the tender bringing
back visitors from the Empress of
Japan, but he did not see Danen-
berg.

At this stage Mr. Haines said that
the case would be adjourned until
Tuesday.

Danenberg, who had been holding
a handkerchief to his face all morn-
ing complained of toothache and
said that he wanted dental treat-
ment and not medical treatment.

Regarding the question of bail,
Mr. Haines said that if Danenberg
could get two sureties which would
satisfy the police he would con-
sider granting bail at the next hear-
ing.

丹嫩伯格第二次出庭
针对一名英国人的盗窃指控继续审理；登上“皇后”号邮轮

昨日，在香港英籍人士卡洛斯·奥兰多·丹嫩伯格第二次出庭，被控盗窃属于伦敦受教育的暹罗医师 C. A. 孙多拉（C. A. Soondora）博士的某些钱款及价值1,000美元的财物。在 registrar（书记官）C. H. 海恩斯先生主持的皇家警察法庭上，呈堂证据涉及被告如何登上加拿大太平洋轮船公司的“日本皇后”号（Empress of Japan）邮轮——表面上是去与一位女友告别——并在船开走后仍留在船上。F. 沃特金·威廉姆斯先生代表检方出庭，而丹嫩伯格未由律师代表。

詹姆斯·鲁普（James Roope），26岁，厨师，无固定住所，称他于1935年9月在救世军招待所首次遇见丹嫩伯格，当时被告正住在那里。后来，证人在与其兄弟同住十天后，前往位于汉口路与云南路拐角处的扬子饭店。在此处，丹嫩伯格向他介绍了两个人，其中一位是孙多拉博士，介绍时使用的是库利奇（Coolidge）博士之名。

另一人被称为梁先生（Mr. Liang）。几天后，丹嫩伯格请他与自己一同住在扬子饭店519室，并与库利奇博士、梁先生、伊拉甘先生（Mr. Ilagan）及被告一起，从2月20日住至4月18日。

被告还将饭店211室用作某种私人办公室，后来作为库利奇博士的起居室。3月22日晚，被告与证人在走廊里徘徊约一小时，讨论211室的租金问题。丹嫩伯格告诉他租金共计109美元，并说会支付这笔钱，补充道他会尽力筹款。后来他说：“别担心，吉姆。这毕竟没多少钱，而且如果我想要，总能弄到钱。”被告随后向证人展示了一堆钱，并补充说：“我现在不太想付房费，因为我希望库利奇博士……”此时证人犹豫了，在被询问时表示他不确定这是否是丹嫩伯格的原话。该句随后被划去。

证人接着说，暂时拖欠房费是丹嫩伯格的主意，目的是让库利奇博士感到难过，希望库利奇博士会设法筹钱支付房租。丹嫩伯格于3月23日离开上海，而在此日期前约两周，他注意到被告持有库利奇博士的护照，据称是交给他保管的。3月22日晚，扬子饭店一楼侍者进入519室向丹嫩伯格索要211室的租金，他回答说“等等”。租金后来支付了。3月22日，库利奇博士因211室被锁而不得不在室外过夜。

女友

3月23日，丹嫩伯格请求证人陪同他去送一位女友登上“日本皇后”号。当被告进入619室时，伊拉甘先生和库利奇博士正熟睡，他身穿一件驼毛大衣。他们离开房间时他锁上了门，随后前往211室。在此处，

被告激动地走来走去，并告诉证人他可以使用库利奇博士的雨衣。丹嫩伯格拿走了属于该医生的一条围巾，而那件驼毛大衣也属于此人。

他们从饭店前往 Sun Co.（音译：桑公司）购买送给女友的礼物，丹嫩伯格支付了5.50美元，随后前往上海与虹口码头，登上了“日本皇后”号。

在接待处，丹嫩伯格询问一位姓宋（Sung）的人的舱位，这使得证人相信那位女友名叫玛丽·宋小姐（Miss Mary Sung）。他们被告知此人在425号舱，但去那里后并未见到任何人。两人一起在船上四处寻找后，丹嫩伯格请证人留在舱内，他自己去楼上看看。在此期间，锣声和汽笛声响起，召唤非乘客上岸，证人跑过船身得以登上码头。他立即前往海关栈桥，以便迎接从“日本皇后”号送回访客的小艇，但他并未见到丹嫩伯格。

此时，海恩斯先生表示案件将延期至周二审理。

丹嫩伯格整个上午都用手帕捂着脸，抱怨牙痛，并称他需要的是牙科治疗而非内科治疗。

关于保释问题，海恩斯先生说，如果丹嫩伯格能找到两名令警方满意的担保人，他将在下次听证时考虑准予保释。

Danenberg's Application
For Bail Is Refused

Briton Facing Larceny Count To Try To Provide
Suitable Sureties During Remand; Accused
Is Not Asked To Plead To Charge

After hearing the evidence of arrest presented by the prosecution, and prior to adjourning the hearing of the case until next Friday, July 1, Magistrate C. H. Haines, in the British Police Court yesterday morning, refused Carlos Orlando Danenberg's application for bail, ordering the Briton to be detained in custody during the period of remand.

Danenberg, alias C. A. Orly, 42-year-old Briton, was arrested on a British Supreme Court warrant on Friday morning by Detective Sub-Inspector John Crighton, of Crime Branch Headquarters, S.M.P. The warrant was issued on April 2, last, upon the complaint made by a Siamese subject, Dr. Char Anusara Soondara, that between March 25 and 27, at Shanghai, Danenberg stole certain articles of clothing, value $1,500 and the sum of $350 in cash, from him, contrary to Section II of the Larceny Act of 1916.

After Mr. Haines, sitting as magistrate, had the charge read out to Danenberg, he informed the accused that he would take the case under preliminary examination, as he did not know, until he heard the evidence, whether or not it was in his power to judge the case. He therefore, did not ask the accused to plead to the charge read out by the Court Marshal.

Danenberg then immediately asked that the case be dismissed and informed the magistrate that the complainant had written to the police requesting them to withdraw the charge. In this respect, at a later stage of the hearing, Magistrate Haines informed the accused that under British law, once a complaint is made, and a warrant issued, a complainant has no power to withdraw same. "You must get it out of your mind," Mr. Haines concluded.

Prosecution Opposes Bail

Under the direct examination of Mr. C. W. Williams, of Hansons, who appeared for the prosecution, Detective Sub-Inspector Crighton related that on April 2, he applied for a warrant on information of complaint and the British Consulate. He was unable to execute it—as the accused had left Shanghai—until 10.30 a.m. June 24, at the Crime Branch Headquarters, S.M.P.

At this stage Mr. Williams, in addressing the magistrate, pointed out that in view of the length of time between the issue of the warrant and apprehension of the accused, that he be detained in custody during the adjournment. "What has happened once, may happen again," he concluded, "I ask the accused to be detained in custody."

"Where are you living now?" the magistrate asked Danenberg.

"I am now in custody of the Police Headquarters," came the reply.

"But, where did you live?"

"In Shanghai. In various hotels," answered the accused.

Danenberg's Statement

Danenberg then asked permission to make an application for bail and make a statement. He informed the magistrate that he had been arrested in connection with the case in Hongkong, detained and then released on $250 bail and two sureties. He also stressed the fact that although he was not extradited, he had voluntarily and on his own free will and accord, and at his own expense, left Hongkong and come to Shanghai.

Magistrate Haines interrupted him at this stage to point out that his object in coming back to Shanghai was to settle the matter with the complainant, and not to surrender himself to the police, which in fact he did not do, until Friday morning. In the course of his statement Danenberg admitted that he went to Hongkong without his passport, which was in the hands of the local passport officer.

Two Objections

Rising again, Mr. Williams placed two objections against bail being granted. First, that as Danenberg had gone to Hongkong not on his own passport, then he must have used that of another, and secondly, that when he returned to Shanghai, he went to the complainant and did not surrender himself to the police.

On hearing the prosecution, Mr. Haines said, addressing Danenberg, "I am afraid I must refuse bail. There is not sufficient guarantee of your coming back at the next hearing."

Prior to adjourning until next Friday, the magistrate informed the accused that if he obtained two sureties, which must be entirely satisfactory to the police, he would grant bail following the next hearing.

丹嫩伯格的保释申请
被驳回

面临盗窃指控的英国人试图在还押期间提供合适的担保人；被告未被要求对指控进行答辩

昨日早晨，在英国警务法庭，海恩斯（C. H. Haines）推事在听取检方提交的逮捕证据后，并在将案件听证会延期至下周五（7月1日）之前，驳回了卡洛斯·奥兰多·丹嫩伯格的保释申请，命令这名英国人在还押期间予以拘留。

丹嫩伯格，又名 C. A. Orly，42岁的英国人，于周五上午由上海公共租界工部局警务处刑事科总部侦探副督察约翰·克莱顿（John Crighton）依据英国最高法院的逮捕令将其逮捕。该逮捕令于去年4月2日签发，系基于一名暹罗籍人士 Char Anusara Soondara 博士的投诉，指控丹嫩伯格于3月25日至27日期间在上海从其处窃取价值1,500美元的衣物及350美元现金，此举违反了《1916年盗窃罪法案》第二条。

海恩斯推事坐堂审案，在向丹嫩伯格宣读指控后，告知被告他将对此案进行初步审查，因为在听取证据之前，他尚不清楚自己是否有权审理此案。因此，他未要求被告就法院法警宣读的指控进行答辩。

丹嫩伯格随即请求驳回此案，并告知推事，原告已致信警方要求撤销指控。对此，在听证会的后续阶段，海恩斯推事告知被告，根据英国法律，一旦提出投诉并签发逮捕令，原告无权撤回。“你必须打消这个念头，”海恩斯先生总结道。

检方反对保释

在代表检方出庭的汉森律师事务所（Hansons）C. W. 威廉姆斯先生的直接讯问下，侦探副督察克莱顿陈述称，他于4月2日根据投诉信息及英国领事馆的申请签发了逮捕令。由于被告已离开上海，他直到6月24日上午10:30才在上海公共租界工部局警务处刑事科总部执行该逮捕令。

此时，威廉姆斯先生在对推事发言时指出，鉴于签发逮捕令与逮捕被告之间时间跨度较长，建议在延期审理期间将其拘留。“发生过一次的事，可能会再次发生，”他总结道，“我请求将被告拘留。”

“你现在住在哪里？”推事问丹嫩伯格。

“我现在被拘押在警察总局，”回答道。

“但是，你之前住在哪里？”

“在上海。住在各家旅馆，”被告回答。

丹嫩伯格的陈述

丹嫩伯格随后请求允许提出保释申请并发表陈述。他告知推事，他曾在香港因本案被捕，被拘留后以250美元保释金及两名担保人获释。他还强调，尽管他未被引渡，但他是自愿、出于自由意志且自费离开香港来到上海的。

海恩斯推事在此阶段打断了他，指出他回到上海的目的是与原告解决此事，而非向警方自首，事实上他直到周五早晨才这样做。在陈述过程中，丹嫩伯格承认他前往香港时未携带护照，其护照在当地护照官员手中。

两点异议

威廉姆斯先生再次起身，对准予保释提出两点异议。第一，既然丹嫩伯格去香港时未使用自己的护照，那么他一定使用了他人的护照；第二，当他返回上海时，他去见了原告，而未向警方自首。

听取检方意见后，海恩斯先生对丹嫩伯格说：“恐怕我必须拒绝保释。没有充分的保证确保你在下次听证时回来。”

在延期至下周五之前，推事告知被告，如果他能获得两名完全令警方满意的担保人，他将在下次听证后准予保释。

Danenberg Bail
Offer Refused
By Magistrate

Briton To Be Detained
To Friday, Day Of
Next Hearing

Remanded in custody to next
Friday by Magistrate C. H. Haines
in the British Police Court yester-
day morning, Carlos Orlando Da-
nenberg, alias C. A. Orly, British,
was refused bail.

Danenberg was arrested on Fri-
day in the French Concession after
a long search, and is accused of
having stolen from Dr. Char A.
Soondora, young London-educated
Siamese physician, property to the
value of $1,000 last March.

In offering bail, Danenberg
stated that he could produce bail
in the form of a surety from the
son of Sir Robert Ho Tung.

Magistrate Haines informed the
accused that he would have to be
detained until the next hearing,
when he would be granted bail if
the sureties he would be able to
produce were satisfactory to the
police.

Asked whether the typewritten
copy of his statement was identical
in wording with the original writ-
ten by him following his arrest.
Danenberg answered in the affirma-
tive.

According to this statement, he
returned to Shanghai to square
matters with the complainant. Ma-
gistrate Haines pointed out that it
seemed the accused was under the
erroneous impression that he could
settle matters with Dr. Soondora
out of court. The charge, he added,
could not be withdrawn.

It is alleged that the property
stolen by the accused consisted of
money, clothing, a banking code
and the physician's passport, after
he recommended that the Siamese
doctor take a room in the Yangtse
Hotel at the corner of Hankow and
Yunnan Roads.

丹嫩伯格保释
遭法官拒绝

英国人将被拘留
至周五下次
聆讯之日

昨日晨，在英国巡捕房法庭，C. H. 海恩斯（C. H. Haines）法官将卡洛斯·奥兰多·丹嫩伯格（Carlos Orlando Danenberg），化名 C. A. 奥利（C. A. Orly），英籍人士，还押候审至下周五，并拒绝其保释申请。

丹嫩伯格于周五在法租界经过长时间搜捕后被捕，被控于今年三月从查尔·A·孙多拉博士（Dr. Char A. Soondora，一位年轻的受过伦敦教育的暹罗医生）处盗窃价值1,000美元的财物。

在提出保释时，丹嫩伯格称他能提供何东爵士（Sir Robert Ho Tung）之子作为担保人。

海恩斯法官告知被告，他必须被拘留至下次聆讯，届时若他能提供的担保人令警方满意，将准予保释。

当被问及他的陈述的打字副本与他被捕后亲笔书写的原件措辞是否一致时，丹嫩伯格给予了肯定回答。

根据该陈述，他返回上海是为了与投诉人了结此事。海恩斯法官指出，被告似乎错误地认为他可以在庭外与孙多拉医生解决此事。他补充说，该项指控不得撤销。

据称，被告盗窃的财物包括现金、衣物、银行密码本以及该医生的护照，此前他曾建议这位暹罗医生入住位于汉口路与云南路拐角处的扬子饭店（Yangtse Hotel）。

page_data.en:
Danenberg Refused
Bail; Will Answer
Charges On Friday

Carlos Orlando Danenberg; alias
C. A. Orly, 42 year old Hongkong
born Britisher, was remanded in
custody until Friday, July 1, this
morning by Mr. C. H. Haines, Re-
gistrar of the British Police Court,
after bail was refused.

Danenberg was arrested yester-
day, on a British Court warrant
issued last March, when he
allegedly obtained from a Siamese
Dr. Char Soondora, property, a
passport and cash to the approxi-
mate value of $1000.

According to the statement of the
accused, he returned to Shanghai
"to fix matters up" with the
alleged victim, and when asked
what bail he could produce, he
said that he could obtain a surety
from the Son of Sir Robert Ho
Tung. Mr. Haines then told the ac-
cused that he would have to remain
in custody until the next hearing
and that he would be granted bail
if the sureties that he may be able
to produce then, would satisfy the
police.

When asked whether the type-
written copy of his statement was
identical in wording with the
original written by him, the ac-
cused said that it was as "Inspec-
tor Orighton and myself worked
together on it."

The Registrar then told the ac-

卡洛斯·奥兰多·丹嫩伯格，化名 C. A. 奥利，42岁，生于香港的英国人，在今早因保释被拒，被英国巡捕房法庭书记官 C. H. 海恩斯先生还押候审至7月1日（周五）。

丹嫩伯格于昨日依据去年三月签发的英国法院逮捕令被捕，当时他被指从暹罗医生查尔·孙多拉（Char Soondora）处获取了价值约1,000美元的财物、护照及现金。

根据被告的陈述，他返回上海是为了与所谓受害者“把事情摆平”，当被问及能提供何种保释时，他说他能获得何东爵士之子作为担保人。随后海恩斯先生告诉被告，他必须继续羁押至下次聆讯，如果届时他能提供的担保人令警方满意，将准予保释。

当被问及他的陈述的打字副本与他亲笔书写的原件措辞是否一致时，被告称是一致的，因为“是奥赖顿（Orighton）巡长和我共同完成的”。

随后书记官告诉被告，后者似乎存在错误印象，以为可以直接与投诉人在庭外解决此事。这是行不通的，因为指控无法撤销。P. W. 威廉姆斯先生（Mr. P.. W. Williams）担任控方，而被告自行辩护。

暹罗人财物被捕

受过伦敦教育的医生
称损失1,000美元

经过长时间搜寻，昨天以盗窃罪逮捕了英籍人士 C. C. 丹嫩伯格（C. C. Danenberg），行动由副督察 J. 克莱顿（J. Crighton）执行。丹嫩伯格在公共租界被收押，并将于今日提堂受审于英国巡捕房法庭。据称，去年三月，在诱使孙多拉医生入住位于汉口路与云南路的扬子饭店（Yangtze Hotel）后，他从这位年轻的、受过伦敦教育的暹罗医生 C. A. 孙多拉（C. A. Soondora）处窃取了总价值1,000美元的各种财物。

据说从初来上海的孙多拉医生处窃取的财物包括现金、衣物、银行密码本以及该医生的护照。

丹嫩伯格昨天在法租界被发现，并被劝往福州路警察总局，在那里被捕。

孙多拉医生来自暹罗北部的清迈（Chiengmai），据称在其国内人脉广泛。

1932年，由于经营不善和债务问题，该医院被拍卖，并由 S. 特雷弗·史密斯（S. Trevor Smith，档案号 I.O. 5371 和 E.251）购得，此人为英籍欧亚混血儿，声誉不佳，是江西路264号519室中国苎麻纺织公司（China Grass Spinning & Weaving Co.）的所有者。据报道，S. 特雷弗·史密斯是应其情妇 F.Y. 丹嫩伯格夫人（Mrs. F.Y. Dannenberg）的要求购买了该医院，后者成为该机构的管理者和名义上的业主。

经营并不成功，上海疗养院不得不向九江路8号的三多洋行银行（Tritoor Bank）借款约3,000美元。贷款协议由 H. Y. 丹嫩伯格夫人签署，并由 S. 特雷弗·史密斯先生担保。由于款项未在到期日偿还，案件移交律师处理，特雷弗·史密斯后来支付了几百美元，并承诺分期偿还余额。据说上海疗养院还向汉口路4号的中国建设银公司（China Finance Corp.）借过款。
